_doc: House trees (SPEC §17): four branches of techniques that live in people. A tech is learned by DOING the activity (learn.* are the qualifications and yearly chances for NPCs; learn.player is the practice the player's own actions count towards), is held by the people who know it and taught by masters to apprentices and children (teach.*), is preserved by scribes in books (writable) and is lost when its last holder dies unrecorded. `requires` are techs the learner must already know (the player's House counts its members). `start` is the share of qualified people who already know it when a run begins (0 = undiscovered). `effects` is a vocabulary other modules read through advancement.bonus()/settlementBonus(); the keys are listed in docs of src/sim/advancement/types.ts. `year` gates the tech until that game year (late techs).

branches.name: Economy
branches.blurb: Ploughs and mills, charters and credit: how the land and the market pay.

branches.name: Military
branches.blurb: Bows, armour, castles and siege engines: how a House holds what it has.

branches.name: Kinship & Diplomacy
branches.blurb: Marriage, oaths and treaties: how Houses bind each other.

branches.name: Knowledge & Belief
branches.blurb: Letters, learning and healing: what the Church and the schools keep alive.

techs.name: Heavy plough
techs.desc: A wheeled plough with coulter and mouldboard turns the heavy clay soils that the scratch-plough cannot. Needs oxen, but every acre yields more.

techs.name: Improved rotation
techs.desc: Peas and beans on the fallow field, manure spread with care: the three-field round is made to feed more mouths.

techs.name: Watermill
techs.desc: A wheel in the stream grinds the village corn faster than a hundred querns. Millers learn to dam, to race and to gear.

techs.name: Windmill
techs.desc: A post mill turned into the wind grinds where there is no stream. New in the lowlands, and the lords' millers are jealous of it.

techs.name: Fulling mill
techs.desc: Water-driven hammers full the cloth in place of the fuller's feet, and a town's wool becomes broadcloth.

techs.name: Market charter
techs.desc: The right to hold a weekly market, written under the lord's seal. Stalls, tolls and the peace of the market follow.

techs.name: Fair charter
techs.desc: A yearly fair of several days draws merchants from far off. The town keeps the tolls and the crowds fill the inns.

techs.name: Guild charter
techs.desc: The masters of a trade swear together, set the quality and the prices, and watch the town by night against fire.

techs.name: Wool trade
techs.desc: English wool is the finest in Christendom: those who grade it, bale it and ship it to the looms of the north grow rich.

techs.name: Letters of credit
techs.desc: A merchant's sealed letter, honoured by his partners in another town, saves carrying silver over robbers' roads.

techs.name: Longbow drill
techs.desc: A bowman who has drawn a war bow since boyhood looses a dozen arrows a minute. Sunday practice at the butts breeds an army of them.

techs.name: Crossbows
techs.desc: A windlass spans the bow and a clerk could shoot it. The Church frowns on it, and every garrison wants it.

techs.name: Coat of plates
techs.desc: Iron plates riveted inside a cloth coat turn arrow and blade. A smith who can make one is a man worth keeping.

techs.name: Plate armour
techs.desc: A full harness of fitted steel from crown to heel. Slow to forge, ruinous to buy, and a knight in it is nearly proof against arrows.

techs.name: Destriers
techs.desc: Great warhorses bred and trained for the couched lance; a charge of them breaks any line that has not stakes.

techs.name: Stone keep
techs.desc: A square tower of dressed stone replaces the timber motte: it cannot be burned, and a few men can hold it for months.

techs.name: Curtain walls
techs.desc: A ring of stone round the whole bailey, with mural towers and a gatehouse. It takes years and a fortune, and it makes the place a fortress.

techs.name: Concentric castle
techs.desc: Wall within wall, each commanding the other, so that a breach of the outer ring leaves the attacker in a killing ground.

techs.name: Trebuchet
techs.desc: A counterweighted beam that hurls a stone the weight of a man against a wall. No curtain wall stands long before one.

techs.name: Paid retinues
techs.desc: Indentured men-at-arms kept in wages by the year, not called out for forty days: the lord's own army.

techs.name: Bombards
techs.desc: Hooped iron tubes that throw stone balls by powder. Loud, slow and dangerous to the gunner, and the end of the high wall.

techs.name: Marriage pacts
techs.desc: Contracts of dowry and dower, drawn up before witnesses, that bind two families and settle who inherits.

techs.name: Wardship
techs.desc: A lord holds the orphan heir of a vassal, keeps the revenues till he comes of age and chooses his bride.

techs.name: Oaths of fealty
techs.desc: Hands joined between a lord's, a vow on relics: the bond on which every vassal's service rests.

techs.name: Truces
techs.desc: The Truce of God, a fortnight's peace, a ransom paid and honoured: a way out of a war that neither can win.

techs.name: Heralds
techs.desc: Men in painted tabards who know every shield in the land, carry challenges under safe-conduct and keep the roll of arms.

techs.name: Tournaments
techs.desc: A mêlée and a joust under rules, with heralds, ladies and ransoms: where young knights win horses, wives and a name.

techs.name: Alliance treaties
techs.desc: A written pact of mutual aid sworn by two Houses, with hostages or marriages as pledge.

techs.name: Council of the realm
techs.desc: Barons, bishops and burgesses summoned to advise the king and grant him taxes: law made by consent.

techs.name: Parish school
techs.desc: The priest teaches a few boys their letters and the creed. A village with a clerk's son is a village that can keep accounts.

techs.name: Scriptorium
techs.desc: A heated room of desks where monks copy books on vellum. What is written there outlives the men who knew it.

techs.name: Cathedral school
techs.desc: Masters lecture on grammar, logic and scripture to the clever sons of the diocese; a few go on to the great studia abroad.

techs.name: University
techs.desc: A guild of masters and scholars with its own privileges, degrees and halls. Law, medicine and theology are taught to all who can pay.

techs.name: Herbal medicine
techs.desc: Herbals and the lore of simples: willow-bark for fever, comfrey for broken bones, rue and wormwood against the pestilence.

techs.name: Infirmary and hospital
techs.desc: Beds, clean linen, broth and a brother who does nothing but nurse: the sick of a whole town can recover under one roof.

techs.name: Charters and records
techs.desc: Rolls of rents, charters sealed in wax and a chest to keep them: a House whose rights are written can prove them.

techs.name: Accounting
techs.desc: Double columns, tallies and the exchequer's chequered cloth: the lord who knows what he has is hard to cheat.

techs.name: Printing
techs.desc: Movable type and a press: a hundred copies in the time a monk copies a page. Learning leaves the cloister for good.
